audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never names a single Zaahen ability. It uses the literal placeholder word 'Ultimate' fifteen times — tldr, winCon, enemyWin, phases[1].why, phases[2].why, phases[5].why, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.trading, breakdown.spikes, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.difficulty, dosFull[0], dosFull[1], dontsFull[0], report[1], report[5], report[9], report[11], report[12], focus.text. The content layer names no ability of his either — it says 'his sustain' and 'his physical burst'.
audit.why: This is the largest matchup in the whole Galio top table by sample size, 1679 games, and the page cannot tell the player what to look at. 'Track Zaahen's Ultimate' is not advice. His abilities are Cultivation of War (P), The Darkin Glaive (Q), Dreaded Return (W), Aureate Rush (E) and Grim Deliverance (R).
audit.corrected: Grim Deliverance is the ultimate, 110/95/80, a rise-and-stab that heals him for part of the damage. The lane-relevant cooldowns are Aureate Rush (E) at 10s and Dreaded Return (W) at 14s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (P Cultivation of War; Q The Darkin Glaive 10/9/8/7/6; W Dreaded Return 14/13.5/13/12.5/12, range 850; E Aureate Rush 10/9.5/9/8.5/8; R Grim Deliverance 110/95/80, range 600)

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late says 'magic-tank scaling and your taunt shrug off Zaahen's physical burst, so he can no longer win the side-lane duel', whys[6] says '2+ items is yours', and spikes[3] says 'MR and taunt blank his physical burst; the duel is flatly yours from here'.
audit.why: Two things in his kit make that false. Aureate Rush carries percent-health damage, which resistances do not reduce — _missing-interactions.json flags exactly this as 'Zaahen bypasses stacking resistances (Aureate Rush) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here'. And Cultivation of War stacks bonus attack damage from every hit on a champion and lets him REVIVE when filled. Stacking MR against a percent-health attacker who comes back from the first kill is the worst possible late-game plan, and the page recommends it three times.
audit.corrected: Aureate Rush deals percent health, so resistances do not blunt it, and Cultivation of War stacks his AD and lets him revive once filled. Late is his, not yours — build health and anti-heal, and never duel him alone at full stacks.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (E Aureate Rush flags: dash, percentHealth; P Cultivation of War: 'gaining bonus Attack Damage per stack. When filled with Determination, Zaahen gains increased Attack Damage and can revive')

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Galio Levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items in a matchup he wins 45.86% of over 1679 games, and it disagrees with the entry's own why-lines at two of those rows: whys[1] calls Level 2 'a skill lane' and whys[2] says 'Level 3 remains even'.
audit.why: 1679 games is the largest sample in this slice, so the win rate is not noise — Galio is behind here. A chart that hands him four of seven rows including the last one is the opposite of what the data says, and the two-plus-item row is exactly where his kit stops working against percent-health damage and a revive passive.
audit.corrected: Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Galio, Zaahen — the five even rows the prose already describes, Galio's first-item window, and the late game to Zaahen.
sources: scratchpad packet galio.json entry zaahen (45.86%, 1679 games)

audit.whatIsWrong: The only sequencing rule on the page is 'never trade while W Shield of Durand is down', repeated in early, spikes[0], whys[1], wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0]. Not one Zaahen cooldown is given, because not one Zaahen ability is named.
audit.why: The rule is right but it is Galio's clock, not his. His clock is what tells you when to step up: Aureate Rush 10/9.5/9/8.5/8 is the dash that reaches you, Dreaded Return 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 is the 850-range pull that starts his combo, The Darkin Glaive is 10s at rank 1, and Grim Deliverance is 110s at rank 1. Shield of Durand is 18s at rank 1, so it is on a longer clock than either of his engage tools — which is the real reason the 'only trade with W' rule bites.
audit.corrected: His engage is Dreaded Return at 14s and Aureate Rush at 10s; your Shield of Durand is 18s. You are on the longer cooldown, so trade only in his downtime and never spend the W first.

audit.whatIsWrong: The highest-value line in _missing-interactions.json for this pairing is absent: 'Your Justice Punch (E) shuts off Zaahen's Aureate Rush (E) — hold it for the engage, not the poke.'
audit.why: Aureate Rush is his only dash and the way he closes on a Galio who is trying to sit at Q range. Justice Punch knocks up, so it is the one button that answers the rush — and the entry currently gives no instruction about when to spend E at all.
audit.corrected: Hold Justice Punch for Aureate Rush. The knockup is your answer to the only dash he has, and spending it on poke leaves you with nothing when he closes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both sides carry displacement and neither layer says so.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags 'knockup-enabler: Both sides carry displacement (Hero's Entrance (R) vs The Darkin Glaive (Q), Dreaded Return (W)) — whoever lands it first owns the trade.' The Darkin Glaive can be recast so his next attack knocks up, and Dreaded Return pulls at 850 range. Against a Galio whose taunt only lands on release, either one cancels the charge, which is precisely why 'trade with W up' is the rule — and the page never explains the mechanism.
audit.corrected: Both his Q recast and his 850-range Dreaded Return displace, and either cancels a charging Shield of Durand before the taunt releases. Start the channel only after one of them is spent.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (Q: 'recast this ability to have his next attack deal bonus damage and knock up his target', flags knockup; W: 'stabs in a direction, damaging enemies hit, then pulls them toward him', flags knockup, range 850)

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions Grievous Wounds, and the full layer's Itemization line is the only Galio entry in this slice without the 'Oblivion Orb early' clause.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal for The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance, and the kit confirms heal flags on both. content.early already frames the lane as 'your Q poke against his sustain' — which is an anti-heal argument that never reaches an item recommendation.
audit.corrected: The Darkin Glaive heals on a 10-second cooldown and Grim Deliverance heals for part of its damage — Grievous Wounds is what makes the chip war winnable.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (Q flags heal; R 'healing for a portion of the damage dealt', flags heal)

audit.whatIsWrong: The Darkin Glaive is not identified as an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags autoreset-burst-tell and the kit confirms the autoReset flag: his next attack slashes twice, and the recast turns the following attack into a knockup. So his opener is a double-hit that arrives on the auto wind-up rather than on a visible cast, and the knockup follows immediately after.
audit.corrected: The Darkin Glaive resets his auto into a double slash and heals him, and the recast makes the next attack a knockup — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast bar.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (Q The Darkin Glaive flags: knockup, heal, autoReset)

notes: This entry had the worst naming problem in the slice: the full layer used the literal placeholder 'Ultimate' in place of Zaahen's ability name in roughly twenty strings, and the content layer named none of his abilities at all. His kit is Cultivation of War (P), The Darkin Glaive (Q), Dreaded Return (W), Aureate Rush (E), Grim Deliverance (R). Many of those placeholder strings — breakdown.mid, breakdown.trading, breakdown.spikes, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.difficulty, report[1], report[9], report[11], report[12], tradeGood, loading — still say 'Ultimate' and need the same substitution; I edited the ones where a length-safe rewrite also carried real information. focus.text is 15 characters and 'Zaahen Grim Deliverance' is 23, outside the band, so I used 'Zaahen Aureate' to at least point at the ability that decides the lane rather than a placeholder. QUESTION for the user is recorded separately about whether the late-game verdict should flip. Zaahen is not covered by the League Wiki checks I used for the rest of the slice — everything here comes from champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json only, and I asserted nothing beyond Riot's own text.
